verdict: Circle grew revenue 20% to $694M as USDC in circulation rose 28% to $77.0B, and it stayed profitable with $55M of net income — though a lower return on reserves capped reserve income growth at 17%.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Total revenue and reserve income was $694M, up from $579M a year ago

kpis.label: USDC in circulation
kpis.note: End of period, up 28% YoY; onchain transaction volume was $21.5 trillion, up 263%

segments.name: Reserve income
segments.note: Interest earned on the cash and U.S. Treasuries backing USDC (a dollar-tracking crypto token). USDC in circulation grew 28%, but the return rate on reserves fell 66 basis points, so income grew only 17%.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Transaction, subscription and services revenue — doubled on growth in subscription and services.

opex.name: Compensation expenses
opex.note: Pay and benefits for staff, including $51.8M of stock-based compensation.

opex.name: General and administrative expenses
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal, finance and admin.

opex.name: Depreciation and amortization expenses
opex.note: Spreading the cost of software, equipment and acquired assets over their useful lives.

opex.name: IT infrastructure costs
opex.note: The computing and systems that run the platform.

opex.name: Digital assets losses (gains)
opex.note: A $0.9M loss — digital assets held in day-to-day operations fell slightly in value.

takeaways.title: USDC kept growing
takeaways.text: USDC in circulation ended the quarter at $77.0B, up 28% YoY, and onchain transaction volume hit $21.5 trillion, up 263% — USDC handled 63% of all stablecoin transaction volume.

takeaways.title: Falling rates bite
takeaways.text: Reserve income grew 17% even though USDC balances grew 28%: the return Circle earns on reserves fell 66 basis points. Reserve income is 94% of all revenue, so it rises and falls with interest rates.

takeaways.title: Profitable again
takeaways.text: Net income was $55M and Adjusted EBITDA $151M (up 24%). Stock pay was $52M — back to normal levels after the IPO-era spike that distorted 2025 comparisons.

oneTimers: Operating expenses include a $7.7M charitable donation of shares to the Circle Foundation, $7.0M of one-off legal expenses and $1.9M of acquisition-related costs — items Circle excludes from its non-GAAP Adjusted EBITDA of $151M.
otherDetail: Other income of $11.7M, net — mainly $13.7M of interest earned on corporate cash and a $5.1M currency gain, partly offset by fair-value losses on convertible debt and derivatives and by losses and impairments on digital assets and strategic investments.
footerNote: Circle's cost of revenue is mostly the cut of reserve income paid to USDC distribution partners like Coinbase.
